clue.text: Stomach support

definitions.meaning: to stomach something is to put up with or tolerate it
a frame or rest that holds something up

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: tolerate (verb) and a holder or rack (noun).

clue.text: One on the telephone to an underwriter?

definitions.meaning: a person who pays to have a phone line
literally one who writes under, signing beneath a document to guarantee it

explanation.definitionFit: A phone customer pays a subscription; someone signing below a document literally writes their name beneath.

clue.text: Island destroyed utterly

indicators.note: uttered or spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: ate as in consumed or destroyed completely

explanation.surface: An island was laid waste completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'when uttered'. An ait is a small river island, as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A small islet in a river is called an ait or eyot.

clue.text: One researching source of disease overwhelming the young eel

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of another
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: an elver is a young eel

explanation.surface: A scientist studies how a disease overwhelms young eels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs deep into a subject is a digger into facts.

clue.text: Mercifully, Lenin let off youth leader

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or spoiled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from youth

explanation.surface: The Soviet leader is said to have spared a young Bolshevik, letting him off with kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LENINLET into LENIENTL; 'leader' of 'youth' adds Y at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with mercy means treating someone gently, not harshly.

clue.text: Stages in development of memoirs on age

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a life is a biography or memoir
a cycle is a long era or age

explanation.surface: Memoirs dwell on the stages of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: The series of phases an organism passes through from birth to death.

clue.text: Stocking-maker's. New Year wish not fulfilled

indicators.note: not completed, so the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: to long for something is to wish for it

explanation.surface: A hosiery maker's New Year hopes come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'stocking-maker is'. 'not fulfilled' removes the last letter from LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are made from this synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Like a woman expecting an enclosure

definitions.meaning: the walled area or curtain wall of a fortification

explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means pregnant, and in castle building means a surrounding fortified wall.

clue.text: One who must remain nameless

parts.note: reads like a secret informant, but describes the word used for a person or thing whose name escapes you

explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word, like whatsit, stands for something whose name is forgotten.

clue.text: Agreement accepted by the old couple

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: An elderly pair give their consent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of oxen is a yoke; to couple is to join two together.

clue.text: How much drink it takes to get Dutch courage?

definitions.text: How much drink it takes to get Dutch courage?

parts.words: How much drink it takes to get Dutch courage
parts.note: Dutch courage is boldness from alcohol; bottle is British slang for nerve, so the measure of drink that fills you with it is a whole container's worth

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a measured quantity of liquor, as much as one glass vessel holds.

clue.text: Make a hit with a metallic sound

definitions.meaning: to be an instant success or get on well with someone
a short sharp noise such as a latch or switch makes

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to become popular or get on at once; the noun is a sharp snapping noise.

clue.text: Disdainful prisoner being sent down

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
moving downwards, going lower

explanation.surface: A scornful inmate has just been jailed, sent down by the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent down' is British slang for being jailed, which fits the prisoner surface; here it simply means going down.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronising behaviour looks down on others with scorn.

clue.text: Embroidery appears to irritate Dot

parts.note: to needle someone is to annoy them
a point is a dot, as a decimal point

explanation.surface: Someone's sewing seems to annoy a woman called Dot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name but is a small mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of stitching on canvas, also called tapestry work.

clue.text: Loves a party with army food

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
rations are soldiers' fixed food allowances

explanation.surface: Someone adores a party with military catering.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship and devotion are kinds of intense love.

clue.text: Orfes seen in Roman times

definitions.meaning: orfes are freshwater fish of the carp family, also called by a three-letter name
in the Roman calendar, certain fixed dates in each month, the 15th or 13th

explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is another name for this European fish; and the Roman calendar marked mid-month days by this term.

clue.text: Cat kept by defendant as familiar

indicators.note: one word is held inside another, the cat sitting within the defendant

parts.note: the person charged in court is the accused
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A defendant's pet cat has grown used to life with its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used to something means it is well known and habitual to you.

clue.text: They dig up old troupers in pantomime

indicators.note: pantomime is chaotic farce, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Veteran actors in a Christmas pantomime are digging up the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pantomime' rearranges O plus TROUPERS. Pantomime is a British Christmas comic stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: People who pull plants out by the roots.

clue.text: Foolish wife omitted from response in English

indicators.note: one letter is left out of the word

parts.note: an answer is a response
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silly wife is left out of an English reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means goose-like, and geese are proverbially silly.

clue.text: Actress appearing to relent, perhaps, absorbed in playing lyre

indicators.note: one set of letters is taken into the middle of another
playing suggests the letters of the instrument are moved about
perhaps signals that the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An actress softens her mood while strumming a lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work here: 'playing' on the instrument and 'perhaps' on relent, one result sitting inside the other. Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian Shakespearean actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Terry was a leading English stage performer of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: It's nearly open for a glass of beer

parts.note: in British slang, a jar is a pint or glass of beer

explanation.surface: The pub is almost opening its doors, just in time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' for a drink is British pub slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to stand this way.

clue.text: Remain a convict as a warning to others

parts.note: to be is to exist or remain
con is short for convict

explanation.surface: A convict is kept on as an example to deter others.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire warns of danger and guides others.

clue.text: Bits of shell used as money

parts.note: bits are pieces or fragments
taken as written
a shell is a light racing boat; an eight is a rowing boat crewed by eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Fragments of seashell once served as currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests the seashell money of old; in rowing it is a racing boat, and an eight is one such boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish silver dollars, pirates' coins, were the historical currency named by this phrase.

clue.text: Bravery award announced for compère

indicators.note: spoken out, so the letters are said rather than written

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal

explanation.surface: A gallantry medal is presented by the host.
explanation.definitionFit: A host presenting a show is a master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Use abusive language in bar

definitions.meaning: to complain bitterly or rant against

explanation.definitionFit: To rant angrily against something; and a horizontal rod.

clue.text: Part of coastal Ibiza required defence

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suspect needs a story placing them somewhere on the Ibiza coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere is the accused's standard plea in court.

clue.text: Volume getting larger — chapter on creeds rewritten

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents put down again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book grows bigger as a chapter about religious beliefs is redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book, but it means loudness. 'rewritten' turns ONCREEDS into RESCENDO after C.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term marks a gradual increase in loudness.

clue.text: Watch out for water sprite

definitions.meaning: a schoolboy warning cry, like cave
a Germanic water spirit or nymph

explanation.definitionFit: A dated British warning shout; and a creature of Germanic folklore living in water.

clue.text: Left one point out of article, showing flexibility

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the is the definite article
a ness is a headland or point of land; out of just leads it on to follow the article

explanation.surface: Someone shows suppleness by deleting a point from an article they wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like a deletion signal, but nothing is removed: the point simply follows the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppleness and agility are what this noun describes.

clue.text: Paperback about former spouse in a series

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: paper as the Sun newspaper, back meaning turned round, giving its letters reversed
an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: A paperback book about an ex-wife is one in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' is one word doing a split job: 'paper' is the Sun, a British tabloid, and 'back' turns it round before it goes about the former spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A connected group or chain of linked things is a nexus.
